item: Home's feed is refreshed when it is three hours old over a grown corpus, and a pass-tail refresh that gives up behind the housekeeping lane runs when the lane ends
summary: The field cache was 12-13 h old on two instances and 'briefing refresh gave up after 900s' appeared 4-7 times per instance. Two causes, both confirmed in code: (1) a Home poll refreshed only after 10% corpus growth, about 20,000 articles on a 200,000-article corpus, more than a day at the measured 9-14 articles a minute; (2) the pass-tail refresh waited at most 900 s behind the housekeeping lane and then skipped its cycle, and a pass lasts about a day. Now (1) a feed older than OO_BRIEFING_MAX_AGE_S (default 3 h, 0 = off) over a corpus grown by at least 25 articles is refreshed on a Home poll under the marker repair's three conditions (memory headroom, scheduler whole-corpus work not running, 600 s after the last refresh finished); (2) a give-up sets _briefing_owed and whichever ends last, the lane (right after releasing the heavy-tail lock) or the thread that gave up (after releasing its own lock), starts that refresh; nothing starts while the scheduler is stopping, an exclusive hold (a restore) is in force or the write-ahead log's pause is on, and the flag stays set for the next lane end or give-up (the pass-tail refresh runs as usual meanwhile); a refused start puts the flag back. The Home-poll age cause also stands aside during the log's pause. Cost: one whole-corpus read about every three hours while Home is open.
